intent: Measure JVM archive compatibility and align fingerprint rules
Measure archive reuse with real application class evidence

name: Archive compatibility study
role: Trains an extracted Spring Boot application and records whether its own class loads from an AppCDS or AOT archive under changed flags and container memory limits.
conditions: JDK 21 and 25 initial runs used an explicit 256 MiB heap and a 1 GiB training container; a successful JVM exit is recorded separately from class-source evidence.

subject: Successful startup is not an archive hit
why: The JVM can start normally after ignoring the archive; the study checks the application class source instead of using exit status alone.

title: Measure actual application class source rather than process success
why: A JVM can exit successfully after falling back to uncached class loading.
alternative: Treat a successful JVM exit as an archive hit — rejected: it misclassifies clean fallback as reuse.

intent: Test reverse archive compatibility and heap layout boundaries

name: JVM archive compatibility matrix
role: Runs baseline, reverse-direction, cgroup-derived heap and pointer-layout scenarios for a Spring Boot application on JDK 21 and 25.
conditions: Application class source is checked against an uncached control. A normal training exit without an archive is recorded as a training failure.

subject: Maximum heap can change pointer layout
why: The 40 GiB maximum heap disabled compressed references and caused archive fallback despite smaller heap-size changes reusing the archive.

title: Ignore SoftMaxHeapSize while retaining conservative heap and GC fields
why: The tested JDK 21 and 25 archives loaded after soft maximum changes in both directions and with G1 and ZGC; a soft target does not itself specify object layout.
alternative: Keep SoftMaxHeapSize in the fingerprint — rejected: tested soft-target changes force unnecessary retraining; remove all heap and GC flags — rejected: measured layout changes invalidate the archive.

intent: Implement the evidence-based fingerprint rule and document profiles

name: Archive compatibility study
role: Trains the extracted Spring Boot application and records actual application-class archive reuse under JVM and cgroup changes.
conditions: Results cover Temurin JDK 21.0.13+9 and 25.0.5+8 on ARM64; they distinguish uncached controls, training failures, and source-line archive hits.

name: JVM fingerprint and archive selection
role: Uses matched Java and Go flag parsing to select the archive fingerprint and preserve explicit profile lookup with safe fallback.
conditions: SoftMaxHeapSize is excluded; maximum and initial heap, GC, RAM percentage, and pointer-layout options remain conservative fingerprint inputs.

subject: Implicit cgroup heap profile changes
why: The measured JVM reused archives across tested cgroup changes when explicit heap options stayed fixed, but implicit heap sizing changed with the cgroup limit. The current fingerprint cannot automatically choose a matching archive profile for that derived heap; explicit profiles work and a miss starts uncached.
